kind: Retrospective method notes, not an original execution transcript

originalProbe.method: Windows Node passed exact helper bytes to isolated WSL Python over stdin. Python wrote a temporary helper and fake browser. Fake normal invocation exited23; --version ignored SIGTERM and slept60 seconds. Node ran original command then diagnostics. Outer Python started Node in a new session, waited7 seconds, killed only that session with SIGKILL after timeout, and checked that a separate foreign session survived.
originalProbe.actualObservation: Original status23 printed; diagnostics did not return within7 seconds; total measured7.010097193997353 seconds; foreign fixture survived.
originalProbe.limitation: The original first driver was executed inline via tool call and was not saved as a standalone local source file. No reconstructed driver is presented as an original. The original raw result and tested helper hash are preserved; exact failing helper bytes were later recovered and verified.

helperRecovery.method: Read bytes from the retained author exact-byte WSL projection, base64 transport to TEMP, verify SHA256 equals the independently executed initial probe hash before writing.
helperRecovery.limitation: Recovered from an already retained exact-byte projection; not recreated from memory, paraphrase or reconstructed source.

fixedRetest.method: Saved Python driver text was executed unchanged via WSL /usr/bin/python3 -c, with stdin JSON containing base64 helper bytes and SHA256. The generated fake retained the original TERM-ignoring --version counterexample and additionally wrote a marker if that branch ran. Outer wait remained7 seconds.
fixedRetest.observed: Original status23 retained; diagnostics returned in1ms, isolated driver measured0.0922834980301559 seconds, version marker absent, diagnostic NOT_RUN retained, foreign fixture survived.
fixedRetest.reproduction: Read the saved driver text and pass it as one literal -c argument to WSL Python. Send one stdin JSON object {helper:<base64 exact fixed helper bytes>,sha:<its SHA256>}. It uses the previously installed /tmp/html-browser-stderr-node-22.18.0/node-v22.18.0-linux-x64/bin/node; that optional environment input must already exist. It never installs or downloads dependencies.
limitations: The saved driver is an actual method artifact from the fixed retest; it is not retroactively substituted for the unsaved first driver.
WSL/Node runtime is an environment prerequisite, not bundled review evidence.
No real Chromium startup, source-root-cause fix, CI approval, model or desktop claim.
